cues.text: Our learning goal is to measure length accurately using useful metric units.
board: Measure length accurately using useful metric units.

board_events.text: Measure length accurately using useful metric units.

cues.text: Success criteria. I can choose a sensible unit and instrument. I can read a ruler from the correct starting point. I can combine metres and centimetres accurately.
board: 1. Choose a sensible unit and instrument.
2. Read a ruler from the correct starting point.
cues.asr_text: SUCCESS CRITERIA I CAN CHOOSE A SENSIBLE UNIT AN INSTRUMENT I CAN READ A RULER FROM THE CORRECT STARTING POINT I CAN COMBINE METERS AND SENTIMETERS ACCURATELY

board_events.text: 1. Choose a sensible unit and instrument.
2. Read a ruler from the correct starting point.

cues.text: Remember that a measure counts equal units. Millimetres help with small details, centimetres suit a pencil, metres suit a room, and kilometres suit a long journey. Choose a tool with useful markings. Smaller units can give a more precise measurement, rather than changing the object.
cues.asr_text: REMEMBER THAT A MEASURE COUNTS EQUAL UNITS MILLIMITORS HELP WITH SMALL DETAILS SENTIMETERS SUIT A PENCIL METERS SUIT A ROOM AND KILOMETRES SUIT A LONG JOURNEY CHOOSE A TOOL WITH USEFUL MARKINGS SMALLER UNITS CAN GIVE A MORE PRECISE MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN CHANGING THE OBJECT

cues.text: A ribbon begins at the two centimetre mark and ends at nine centimetres. Predict its length. Count the equal one-centimetre intervals between those marks, rather than reading the final label alone.
cues.asr_text: A RIBBON BEGINS AT THE TWO CENTIMETER MARK AND ENDS AT NINE CENTIMETERS PREDICT ITS LENGTH COUNT THE EQUAL ONE CENTIMETER INTERVALS BETWEEN THOSE MARKS RATHER THAN READING THE FINAL LABEL ALONE

cues.text: There are seven centimetres between the marks. Nine minus two equals seven. Moving the ruler does not stretch the ribbon: subtract the starting reading whenever the object is not lined up with zero.
cues.asr_text: THERE ARE SEVEN CENTIMETERS BETWEEN THE MARKS NINE MINUS TWO EQUAL SEVEN MOVING THE RULER DOES NOT STRETCH THE RIBBON SUBTRACT THE STARTING READING WHENEVER THE OBJECT IS NOT LINED UP WITH ZERO

cues.text: A display board measures two metres and thirty-five centimetres. We want a single centimetre reading. One metre contains one hundred centimetres, so the two metres account for two hundred centimetres.
cues.asr_text: A DISPLAY BOARD MEASURES TWO METRES AND THIRTY FIVE CENTIMETERS WE WANT A SINGLE CENTIMETER READING ONE METRE CONTAINS ONE HUNDRED CENTIMETERS SO THE TWO METRES ACCOUNT FOR TWO HUNDRED CENTIMETERS

cues.text: Add the remaining thirty-five centimetres. Two hundred plus thirty-five makes two hundred and thirty-five centimetres. The combined measure and the single-unit measure describe exactly the same length.
cues.asr_text: ADD THE REMAINING THIRTY FIVE CENTIMETERS TWO HUNDRED PLUS THIRTY FIVE MAKES TWO HUNDRED AND THIRTY FIVE CENTIMETERS THE COMBINED MEASURE AND THE SINGLE UNIT MEASURE DESCRIBES EXACTLY THE SAME LENGTH

cues.text: Reading nine centimetres as the ribbon length ignores where it started. Count the space between the marks. A different starting mark changes the subtraction, but not the physical ribbon.
cues.chapter: Read the distance, not just the end
board: End reading is not always the length
cues.asr_text: READING NINE CENTIMETERS AS THE RIBBON LENGTH IGNORES WHERE IT STARTED COUNT THE SPACE BETWEEN THE MARKS A DIFFERENT STARTING MARK CHANGES THE SUBTRACTION BUT NOT THE PHYSICAL RIBBON

board_events.text: End reading is not always the length

cues.text: A strip starts at three centimetres and ends at eleven centimetres. How long is it? Look at the model, and keep your prediction in mind.
cues.asr_text: A STRIP STARTS AT THREE CENTIMETERS AND ENDS AT ELEVEN CENTIMETERS HOW LONG IS IT LOOK AT THE MODEL AND KEEP YOUR PREDICTION IN MIND

cues.text: Eleven minus three is eight centimetres. Check by counting eight equal intervals, or placing a zero-start ruler beside the same strip.
cues.asr_text: ELEVEN MINUS THREE IS EIGHT CENTIMETERS CHECKED BY COUNTING EIGHT EQUAL INTERVALS OR PLACING A ZERO START RULER BESIDE THE SAME STRIP

cues.text: Choose a useful unit, read the interval size and check the starting mark. For a practical investigation, measure a pencil in centimetres and millimetres. Discuss which reading describes its length more precisely. Reflect on which model helped you and why. Now try the MathMagic practice, and explain your thinking to someone.
